paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: An aviation inspector is not a 'fix the plane' position but an inspection position that verifies aircraft and maintenance processes against regulations and standards and makes airworthiness determinations: verifying that maintenance and modification work completed by maintenance personnel conforms to standards and procedures, reviewing maintenance records and flight logs to confirm that inspections and overhauls were performed on schedule, inspecting newly built and repaired and modified aircraft to identify damage or defects and assess airworthiness and conformity, examining landing gear and tires and fuselage and wings and engine exteriors for damage or corrosion, and on that basis making the decision to issue or refuse to issue airworthiness documents; people who only want to release aircraft on experience and are unwilling to be responsible for inspection conclusions and release decisions are not suited.

Signals to keep exploring: you can check item by item against checklists and regulatory provisions and record evidence truthfully, are willing to make judgments based on manufacturer and airworthiness documents and technical data and keep traceable inspection and test records, can stop to gather evidence and escalate when the extent of damage, the scope of corrosion, or the basis for conformity is unclear, and are willing to communicate with maintenance personnel, operators, and manufacturers about defects and rectification requirements.

Conditions for pausing investment first: you have not yet completed one full closed loop of record review — on-site inspection — measurement and testing — determination — record filing under any supervised conditions, or you can only express interest by 'liking planes'; also do not treat maintenance-repair experience or being able to fly a plane as proof that you can independently make airworthiness determinations or issue documents. Airworthiness determination, release signing, accident investigation, and unmanned aircraft compliance inspection must be carried out by personnel with the corresponding authorization according to applicable regulations and institutional procedures with traceable basis retained; this page does not provide inspection, determination, or release instructions.

Education and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists 53-6051.01 as Job Zone Three (SVP 6.0 to <7.0); of the published education composition, 34% require an associate or other two-year degree, 29% require a high school diploma or equivalent, and 20% require a postsecondary certificate; most occupations in this zone require vocational school training, related on-the-job experience, or an associate degree, and require prior related work skills and one to two years of training. On the U.S. side the inspection and release authority comes from the authorization and appointment of the competent authority (see the FAA airworthiness certification explanation and the provisions of 14 CFR Part 65 on mechanics and inspection authorization IA). Education, coursework and training, industry certification, institutional internal job qualification, and inspection authorization are different statuses and must be verified item by item by employer, position, and jurisdiction.

One sentence: This is a technical inspection position centered on regulatory conformity verification, on-site inspection evidence gathering, and airworthiness determination, with the core being record review, on-site inspection and measurement and testing, defect determination, the decision to release or refuse, and inspection records, rather than an interest in aircraft or repair craftsmanship.

The work of aviation inspectors can be divided into three categories: inspection and verification (verifying that the maintenance, modification, or repair and overhaul work performed by maintenance personnel conforms to standards and procedures; reviewing maintenance records and flight logs to judge whether inspections and overhauls were performed on schedule; inspecting newly built and repaired and modified aircraft to identify damage or defects and using checklists, hand tools, and test instruments to assess airworthiness and conformity; inspecting landing gear, tires, and the fuselage, wings, and engine exteriors for signs of damage or corrosion and whether repair is needed; and inspecting whether aircraft inspection access panels and doors are securely fastened); testing and determination (starting aircraft and observing instruments and other indicators to find signs of malfunction; performing flight test programs, testing equipment, instruments, and systems under a variety of conditions; making the judgment to issue or refuse to issue airworthiness documents on that basis; and recommending the replacement, repair, or modification of aircraft equipment); and investigation, rules, and training (investigating aviation accidents and complaints to determine the cause; analyzing training programs and conducting oral and written examinations to verify the competence of personnel who operate, install, and repair aircraft equipment; recommending changes to rules, policies, standards, and regulations based on operating conditions and aircraft improvements; and inspecting whether unmanned aircraft systems such as drones conform to safety and operating regulations). All three task categories are premised on stopping to gather evidence and escalating when the basis for conformity is unclear, the work exceeds the authorized scope, or a safety-affecting defect is found.

O*NET53-6051.01 is defined as inspecting aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigation aids, and air traffic control and communications equipment for conformance to federal safety regulations. O*NET detailed data lists 14 tasks: 10 Core, 3 Supplemental, 1 New; drone compliance is New with no Importance, so it cannot be classified under the existing Supplemental. 41 work activities with Importance: conformity judgment 99, equipment inspection 98, documenting 92, identifying 90, updating knowledge and computer use 88. They are group importance, not frequency of occurrence or an individual threshold. In the U.S., airworthiness certificates are issued by FAA Aviation Safety Inspectors or Part183 authorized representatives, and airworthiness certificate rules fall under Part21 Subpart H; an employer's internal quality-inspection authorization does not automatically carry that power. The Part65 mechanic IA is a different authorization: §65.95 allows approval for return to service after certain major repairs or modifications (excluding aircraft under a Part121 continuous airworthiness maintenance program) and annual or progressive inspections, but does not directly grant airworthiness certificate issuance authority.

entries: Record review and verification | Make the basis clear | Pull work orders and maintenance records and flight logs, verify whether inspections and overhauls were performed on schedule, and write out clearly the item inspected and the basis documents.

On-site inspection and evidence gathering | Make findings traceable | Check maintenance work and aircraft condition against the checklist, inspect landing gear and tires and fuselage and wings and engine exteriors for damage or corrosion, and record findings and evidence.

Measurement and testing | Make the judgment supported | Measure and test with tools and instruments, start the aircraft per procedure and observe instruments, perform or witness flight tests and ground tests, and record measured values and results.

Determination and signing | Make the authority clear | Record the conformity conclusion per appointment and duties. Airworthiness certificate issuance by an FAA inspector or authorized representative is verified separately from the mechanic IA's specific return-to-service approval and annual inspection, and is not automatically inferred from a company quality-inspection position or education.

Accident and complaint investigation | Make the cause traceable | Investigate aviation accidents and complaints, collect and preserve evidence, and record conclusions and the parts still to be confirmed.

Collaboration and authorization | Make responsibility attributable | Collaborate with maintenance and operators and manufacturers; carry out airworthiness determination, release signing, accident investigation, and drone compliance through the authorized process, and report open items truthfully.

The O*NET page explicitly labels this wage and the employment and industry data as 'Wage data for Transportation Inspectors', that is, taken from the same family occupation 53-6051.00 and not from 53-6051.01 itself; the median does not equal the entry-level wage and does not constitute an income promise. Pull work orders and maintenance records and flight logs → check maintenance work and aircraft condition against the checklist → inspect and measure with tools and instruments and identify damage or defects → judge conformity against manufacturer and airworthiness documents → record evidence and the basis for the judgment → explain defects and rectification requirements to maintenance personnel and operators.

The precise Chinese occupational wage remains insufficient evidence. Mainland China's revised Civil Aviation Law of 2025 takes effect on 2026-07-01: Article 4 provides that the civil aviation competent department and regional bodies supervise according to law; Articles 25/28 allow design and production organizations to accept commissioned technical inspections, Article 30 covers repair organization licensing, Article 31 covers airworthiness certificates and other flight conditions, and Article 33 provides that repair be performed by licensed organizations or personnel. Articles 36/37 on aviation personnel training, assessment, and licensing requirements must be distinguished by the positions listed, and a uniform license cannot be inferred from the name 'aviation inspector', nor can the FAA IA be applied to China. The precise Chinese classification mutual recognition for this U.S. subdivision, individual inspector appointment, and the national wage distribution were not obtained. Collaborate with maintenance technicians, aircraft operators, manufacturers and designers, and other professional positions within the competent authority; when airworthiness determination, release signing, accident investigation, and unmanned aircraft compliance inspection are involved, handle them according to applicable regulations and institutional authorization, do not decide on one's own, and stop and escalate when the basis is unclear or the work exceeds authorization.

Aviation inspectors focus on conformity inspection of aircraft and maintenance processes and equipment and communications and navigation facilities and on making airworthiness determinations; transportation inspectors cover inspection of broader transport modes such as rail and road and pipelines; motor vehicle inspectors inspect motor vehicles and equipment systems other than aircraft; aircraft mechanic technicians focus on actually performing repair and modification and usually do not issue airworthiness documents; avionics technicians focus on installing and servicing avionics equipment; building and construction inspectors focus on building code conformity inspection; government property inspectors and investigators focus on government property and contract conformity inspection. Adjacent occupations share inspection and record and safety fundamentals, but the object, deliverable, and authorization differ.
A verifiable, traceable, reviewable conformity conclusion

Complete inspection and measurement and testing per procedure, and leave an inspection record that states the item inspected and the basis documents, the inspection and measurement results, the defect and conformity judgment, the reasons for release or refusal, and the parts that remain uncertain, so that a supervisor or reviewer can judge from it.
Inspection records and airworthiness determination and release documents

The object is the aircraft and its components and maintenance processes, as well as air navigation aids, air traffic control, and communications equipment; the basis is airworthiness and technical data, manufacturer and maintenance manuals, and the applicable airworthiness and operating regulations and institutional inspection procedures.

Aviation inspectors (O*NET 53-6051.01 on the U.S. side, Aviation Inspectors) inspect aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigation aids, air traffic control, and communications equipment to ensure conformance with federal safety regulations. The original official duty text is 'Inspect aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigational aids, air traffic controls, and communications equipment to ensure conformance with Federal safety regulations.'; O*NET lists 14 official tasks (10 of them core), including verifying that the maintenance and modification and repair and overhaul work performed by maintenance personnel conforms to standards and procedures (importance 93), reviewing maintenance records and flight logs to judge whether inspections and overhauls were performed on schedule (90), inspecting newly built and repaired and modified aircraft to identify damage or defects and assess airworthiness and conformity (89), issuing or refusing to issue airworthiness documents (89), compiling and maintaining detailed repair and inspection and investigation and certification records and reports (86), inspecting landing gear and tires and fuselage and wings and engine exteriors (86), recommending the replacement and repair or modification of aircraft equipment (79), starting aircraft and observing instruments to find signs of malfunction (79), inspecting whether inspection access panels and doors are securely fastened (77), recommending changes to rules and policies and standards and regulations (57); supplemental tasks include investigating aviation accidents and complaints to determine the cause (93), analyzing training programs and organizing oral and written examinations to verify personnel competence (76), and performing flight test programs to test equipment and instruments and systems (74), plus one new task — inspecting whether unmanned aircraft systems such as drones conform to safety and operating regulations (no importance score is published for this new task). This occupation is in Job Zone Three (SVP 6.0 to <7.0) in the U.S.; its wage and employment and industry data are, as noted on the O*NET page, taken from the same family occupation 53-6051.00. On the mainland China side this page obtained no public occupational entry precisely equivalent to it, so it does not claim precise Chinese duties or admission requirements. This page does not constitute inspection, determination, or release instructions; the relevant decisions must be made by personnel with the corresponding authorization according to applicable regulations and institutional procedures.
Record review — inspection — measurement and testing — determination — recording

Review records and work orders → conduct on-site inspection against the checklist and gather evidence → measure and test with tools and instruments → judge conformity against the basis documents → make the release or refusal decision and state the reasons → file and explain open items.
A reviewable inspection and determination record

The item inspected and the basis documents, the inspection and measured values, the findings and defect description, the conformity judgment and replacement plan, the reasons for release or refusal, and the parts that remain uncertain.
Self and the authorized supervisor (or reviewer)

Inspection conclusions and airworthiness determinations are undertaken by the person according to authorization; when airworthiness release signing, approval for return to service after major repair or modification, accident investigation conclusions, and unmanned aircraft compliance determinations are involved, they are made by personnel with the corresponding authorization according to applicable regulations and procedures, and work must stop and escalate when the basis is unclear or the work exceeds the authorized scope.
Education and preparation

O*NET lists 53-6051.01 as Job Zone Three (SVP 6.0 to <7.0); most occupations in this zone require vocational school training, related on-the-job experience, or an associate degree, and require prior related work skills, knowledge, or experience, with training usually one to two years and an accredited apprenticeship program possibly available; of the published education composition, 34% require an associate or other two-year degree, 29% require a high school diploma or equivalent, and 20% require a postsecondary certificate. The O*NET page shows that this occupation has no registered training program nationwide, and it lists several industry certifications (such as ETA International's fiber optics and ARINC fiber optics certifications, ASTM International's foreign object elimination certification, the North American Transportation Management Institute's safety director and safety supervisor certifications, and the National Business Aviation Association's certified aviation manager). On the mainland China side it is mainly education in aircraft repair and airworthiness-related specialties and job training, with specific requirements set by the employer.
Not mutually substitutable

Education, coursework and training, industry certification, registered apprenticeship experience, institutional internal job qualification, and inspection authorization are different statuses: education does not bring inspection or release authorization, and certification does not mean one can independently make airworthiness determinations, approve return to service after major repair or modification, or conduct inspection work at any location.

At minimum, check six items before onboarding: the occupational definition and the employer entity (O*NET 53-6051.01 is the U.S. definition; on the mainland China side the position and employer must be identified); education and specialized training; institutional internal job qualification and the scope of inspection and release authorization; the working procedures for inspection and measurement and testing; the authorization requirements for airworthiness determination and release signing and accident investigation; and the employment arrangement and compensation definition.
Occupational definition

On the U.S. side it is O*NET 53-6051.01 (Aviation Inspectors); this occupation's wage, employment, and industry data are, as noted on the O*NET page, taken from the same family occupation 53-6051.00 (Transportation Inspectors). On the mainland China side this page obtained no public occupational entry precisely equivalent to this occupation, and the position must first be identified as regulatory-agency inspection, manufacturer quality and airworthiness inspection, operator maintenance quality inspection, or third-party inspection and compliance inspection, because the authorization scope and working procedures differ greatly across employers.
Education and specialized pathway

On the U.S. side the education composition is mainly an associate or two-year degree (of the education composition published on the O*NET page, 34% require an associate or other two-year degree, 29% require a high school diploma or equivalent, and another 20% require a postsecondary certificate), and most positions require prior related work skills and one to two years of training; the O*NET page shows that this occupation has no registered training program nationwide. In mainland China it is mainly education in aircraft repair and airworthiness-related specialties and job training, with specific education requirements set by the employer.
Job qualification and inspection authorization

Inspection and determination and release must follow institutional authorization and applicable regulations. On the U.S. side, airworthiness document issuance requires inspecting the aircraft and reviewing airworthiness data per FAA airworthiness certification requirements (see the FAA 'How Does the FAA Certify Aircraft?'); 14 CFR Part 65 sets out the certification of airmen other than flight crewmembers, where Subpart D sets out the privileges and limitations of mechanics, §65.81 requires that a certificated mechanic must not approve for return to service work for which the mechanic is not familiar, and §65.91–§65.95 set out the qualification, validity period, renewal, and limitations of privileges of inspection authorization (IA). The O*NET certification page separately lists several industry certifications such as fiber optics and foreign object elimination and safety director. On the mainland China side this page obtained no precisely equivalent public occupational entry and admission basis, so before onboarding, check pre-job training and inspection and release authorization, which cannot be inferred directly from education or certification.
Equipment and site safety

The working environment must meet applicable safety requirements (hangar and apron and working-at-height protection, aircraft power-on and fuel system and ground equipment hazardous energy control, noise and contaminant and temperature exposure protection, and foreign object and tool and parts management). O*NET work context shows 98% use email every day, 94% have telephone conversations every day, 88% have face-to-face discussions every day, 84% have physical proximity within arm's length, 51% use specialized protective or safety equipment at least once a week, 41% are exposed to hazardous conditions at least once a month, 33% are exposed to contaminants every day, 32% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise at least once a week; 69% consider the consequences of error extremely serious. This page does not constitute inspection, determination, or release instructions.
Shifts and working hours

Work context shows 68% of typical workweeks are 40 hours, 79% must make decisions every day, 59% have a lot of decision freedom, 58% have a lot of freedom over tasks and priorities and goals, 60% consider repeating the same tasks extremely important, 20% face time pressure every day; common arrangements include on-site inspection scheduling, field work, and duty shifts. When comparing positions, put the employment arrangement, field work arrangement, and overtime arrangements into the written conditions.
Continuing training and review

Airworthiness and operating regulations, inspection techniques and tools, unmanned aircraft rules, and digital inspection and recording tools update fairly quickly (O*NET lists 15 technology skill categories, 12 of them flagged as hot technologies, and the page gives occurrence shares from employer job postings: Microsoft Office 8%, IBM WebSphere MQ 6%, Microsoft Excel 6%, Microsoft PowerPoint 3%, Microsoft Word 2%, with the rest unpublished), requiring continuous continuing training and maintenance of basis documents; confirm before onboarding the training arrangements, inspection authorization, and review mechanism.

paragraphs: All six directions share inspection and record and safety fundamentals as a background, but the inspection object and basis and authorization boundary differ; the same segment of inspection or repair experience cannot be directly converted into another direction's job qualification, certification, or inspection authorization, and this page only compares the duty differences under the public definitions.

The comparison basis is the official occupational description of O*NET 53-6051.01 and the related occupation list on the O*NET page, as well as the adjacent occupation relationships noted in the routing material; an adjacent relationship only indicates proximity of duties and does not mean qualifications, certifications, or authorizations are interchangeable.

The table below compares aviation inspectors and five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and output, key differences, and which option is more suitable for each preference.

The object covers broader transport modes such as rail and road and pipelines and aviation, with a wider inspection scope; aviation inspectors focus on the conformity of aircraft and maintenance procedures and air traffic control and communications and navigation equipment.

If you want to cover multiple transport modes, compare transportation inspectors first; if you want to focus on the aviation field and make airworthiness determinations, aviation inspectors are suitable.
Conduct conformity and safety inspection of multiple transport modes, with the output mainly being cross-mode inspection records and rectification requirements.
Aviation inspectors and transportation inspectors

The inspection object is motor vehicles and equipment and systems other than aircraft, and usually does not involve airworthiness determination; the aviation inspector's object is aircraft and their maintenance processes and aviation facilities.

If you would rather inspect motor vehicles and ground equipment systems, compare motor vehicle inspectors first; if you would rather do aircraft and airworthiness determination, aviation inspectors are suitable.
Inspect the safety and compliance of motor vehicles and equipment systems, with the output mainly being vehicle and equipment inspection records.
Aviation inspectors and motor vehicle inspectors

Focuses on actually performing repair and modification and usually does not issue airworthiness documents; aviation inspectors focus on inspecting maintenance work and making airworthiness determinations and release or refusal decisions.
If you would rather work hands-on repairing aircraft, compare aircraft mechanic technicians first; if you would rather make inspection and release determinations, aviation inspectors are suitable.
Perform aircraft repair and modification, with the output mainly being repair and inspection release records.
Aviation inspectors and aircraft mechanic technicians

Focuses on installing and servicing avionics equipment and usually does not undertake airworthiness determination and release signing; aviation inspectors focus on conformity inspection and determination of aircraft and equipment.
If you would rather install and service avionics equipment, compare avionics technicians first; if you would rather make airworthiness determinations, aviation inspectors are suitable.
Install and service avionics and electrical systems, with the output mainly being equipment servicing and test records.
Aviation inspectors and avionics technicians
The basis is building and construction codes, and the object is buildings and construction processes; the aviation inspector's object is aircraft and aviation facilities and maintenance processes.
If you would rather do building code inspection, compare building and construction inspectors first; if you would rather do aircraft and airworthiness inspection, aviation inspectors are suitable.
Inspect buildings and construction processes against building codes, with the output mainly being construction inspection and rectification records.
Aviation inspectors and building and construction inspectors

The object is government property and contract conformity, and usually does not involve airworthiness technical determination; aviation inspectors focus on technical conformity inspection of aircraft and facilities.

If you would rather do government property and contract inspection, compare government property inspectors and investigators first; if you would rather do aviation technical inspection, aviation inspectors are suitable.
Inspect government property and contract performance, with the output mainly being property and contract inspection records.
Aviation inspectors and government property inspectors and investigators

Conclusion: The basis for choosing a direction is the inspection object and basis and authorization boundary, not whether aviation is involved; once the direction is set, the target direction's training, certification, job qualification, or inspection and release authorization requirements should be checked item by item.

In the U.S., airworthiness certificates are issued by FAA Aviation Safety Inspectors or Part183 authorized representatives, and airworthiness certificate rules fall under Part21 Subpart H; an employer's internal quality-inspection authorization does not automatically carry that power. entries.answer: Verify aircraft and maintenance processes against regulations and basis documents: check whether the maintenance and modification and repair and overhaul work performed by maintenance personnel conforms to standards and procedures, review maintenance records and flight logs, inspect newly built and repaired and modified aircraft to identify damage or defects and assess airworthiness, inspect landing gear and tires and fuselage and wings and engine exteriors, measure and test with tools and instruments, make the decision to issue or refuse to issue airworthiness documents, and compile inspection and investigation and certification records; the specific authorization scope is determined by the institution and the competent authority.
entries.question: What do aviation inspectors do every day?

entries.answer: Mainly hangar and apron and working-at-height and ground equipment handling injuries, exposure to aircraft power-on and fuel systems and hazardous energy, leakage of inspected-unit and operations and maintenance data, injuries from inspection conditions and tool use, loss of control over inspection records and evidence custody, and unauthorized signing and release and missing review mechanisms; the control approach is to work per applicable regulations and institutional procedures and to stop and escalate when the basis is unclear or the work exceeds authorization.
entries.question: What risks should I pay attention to in advance with this job?

entries.answer: Look at reviewable output: whether you can complete inspection and measurement and determination per regulations and procedures and record truthfully, whether you can reason about defects and conformity from the basis documents, and whether you can stop and escalate when the basis is unclear or the work exceeds authorization. The CRI interest code and work styles only indicate that the direction is close and cannot replace this hands-on evidence.
entries.question: How do I judge whether I am suited to being an aviation inspector?

entries.answer: AI and automation can change document retrieval and regulation and manual lookup, measurement records and parameter comparison, and the organization of inspection reports and release text; but the conformity judgment, defect determination, airworthiness release decision, accident investigation conclusion, and drone compliance determination are still undertaken by the person per institutional authorization and applicable regulations. The degree of task automation does not equal a change in the number of positions.
entries.question: Which tasks will AI change?

entries.answer: Conformity and defect determination, the decision to release or refuse airworthiness, approval for return to service after major repair or modification, accident investigation conclusions, and drone compliance determinations must be undertaken by authorized personnel per applicable regulations and institutional procedures; system output can only serve as a rollback-able, reviewable auxiliary step and must be checked against actual measurement and the basis documents.
entries.question: Which steps must keep human review?

subject.summary: Aviation inspectors inspect aircraft and maintenance procedures and air navigation aids and air traffic control and communications equipment against regulations and basis documents: verifying maintenance work, reviewing maintenance records and flight logs, inspecting aircraft, assessing airworthiness, and measuring and testing and making airworthiness determinations. On the U.S. side this corresponds to O*NET 53-6051.01 (Aviation Inspectors), in Job Zone Three (SVP 6.0 to <7.0); its wage, employment, and industry data are, as noted on the O*NET page, taken from the same family occupation 53-6051.00 (Transportation Inspectors). On the mainland China side this page obtained no public occupational entry and national wage distribution precisely equivalent to this occupation, so it does not claim a precisely equivalent Chinese duty or admission requirement, nor does it publish a precise occupational wage for it.
